chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The Jews and the Christians, when they testify, then they become Muslims, their testimonies are accepted.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Are the testimonies of converted Jews and Christians accepted in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of al-Sakuni, establishes that the testimony of Jews and Christians is legally valid immediately upon their conversion to Islam, without requiring a probationary period. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that conversion purifies one's religious status for legal purposes, aligning with the broader concept of 'sahh al-shahada' (validity of testimony) for new Muslims. It highlights the continuity of their legal standing despite their previous distinct dhimmi status.
